Hint 1: Consider what one-hot encoding does to categorical variables. It creates binary columns for each category, where a '1' indicates the presence of that category and a '0' indicates its absence.

Hint 2: Since the sex column has two categories (male and female), one-hot encoding will result in two new columns: $$sex_{male}$$ and $$sex_{female}$$. Each row will have a '1' in one of these columns and a '0' in the other, depending on the value in the original sex column.
